title: Silksong is getting a free expansion in 2 weeks
content: In a "Cherry Time!" presentation , Hollow Knight developer Team Cherry has just revealed a first look at its much-anticipated first content update to Hollow Knight: Silksong. The nautical-themed Sea of Sorrow will come as a free update on December 11. Team Cherry said that Sea of Sorrow will contain multiple new areas, power-ups, and bosses, while I clocked at least three new friendly NPCs in the trailer: A townsperson, a new shopkeeper, and a ferryman. Area-wise, I made out three distinct tilesets in the trailer: A rain-blasted fishing town on the water, a harrowing climb with an electrical storm element, and a green space reminiscent of the early game Bell Bottom. At least the first of these areas appears to be built on cut content for Silksong: "Pharloom Bay" is well-documented on the Hollow Knight wiki , and would have been located on the east side of the map, near the thematically-similar Greymoor. Some elements in the trailer correspond to ones documented by the wiki, like an underwater submersible vehicle, or a scientific lab in the electrical storm area. Which all sounds rad to me, particularly the submersible. Among the all-timer videogame level concepts, "underwater techbase" is one of my very favorites, and Team Cherry seem to be approaching these concepts with a Lovecrafty, Innsmouth flair that reminds me of the Fishing Village zone from Bloodborne. Silksong is already a massive game, and I'm curious as to how Sea of Sorrow will fit both the map, and the game's overall flow from act to act. title: Vermintide 2 mod tools get a public release, and the game's 90% off on Steam too
summary: Holy Sigmar, bless this ravaged body.
content: Though Vermintide 2's had a Steam Workshop since 2018, it's mostly used for quality-of-life stuff like UI tweaks. That's set to change now that Fatshark has announced a public release of its internal developer tools, which they say "will allow modders to work their magic on both editing and creating anything from custom levels, models, textures, particles, animations, and more!" Right now, only a select number of sanctioned mods can be used in Vermintide 2's "official realm" which is the one with loot and leveling that carries over, while unsanctioned mods can only be accessed in a "modded realm" where there are no progression systems. Obviously that's off-putting to a lot of players, so Fatshark has announced a change. "We have an update releasing in early December which will see the Modded Realm have its own, local, offline progression. That means that playing in the Modded Realm will still result in you gaining loot and experience, but said progression will not reflect on the Official Realm. This should make playing on the Modded Realm feel much better and not be discouraging for those that want to try out all of the unsanctioned mods, both the ones that already exist and the ones to come thanks to the Mod Tools!" I'm not sure how many players will be happy to start over from level one just to get access to a wider variety of mods, but I hope it encourages some folks to check them out. Another thing that'll encourage new players is that XP has been doubled from now through till Monday, and Vermintide 2 is on sale for 90% off on Steam . The DLC has been discounted too. In less good news, the servers for Versus Mode are being turned off. "We have monitored the use of the dedicated Versus servers lately," Fatshark said, "and come to the conclusion that they are barely used. We have therefore decided to shut these down." Versus Mode will still be playable, but via the menu option for a custom game or the lobby browser. You'll have to find a crew to play with on Discord first, which is how everyone seems to play Versus at the moment anyway. That shutdown is planned for early December, at the same time as the update that adds local progression to the modded realm. That update will also include balance changes to buff some unpopular talents, new weapon icons, and a Tome of Triumphs in the hub area that will point you at any event if there's a live one, or to the weekly event mode if there isn't. The next event planned is the annual return of Gifts of the Wolf Father in December. Finally, Fatshark mentioned that focusing on the mod tools to get them ready for public release had to take priority from other updates. "The weapon pack and the level that we mentioned in the past has been put on hold," they wrote. "We still want to get back to that, especially the weapon pack, but for now there is no active development on that. It’s important for us that we have transparency here, and while we are not working on these things, we do stick with our games! We have plans both near and far for Vermintide 2." title: Skate is dropping seasons and season passes in favor of 'regular, agile content updates'
summary: The fifth season of Skate will be its last as developer Full Circle looks to try something new.
content: A little over a year after EA launched Skate into early access—where it remains—developer Full Circle is removing the seasonal structure that has underpinned the game so far, saying that doing so will give the team "the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle." Skate got off to a bit of a rough start when it went live in September 2025, and while it's turned around the initially iffy response from players, it hasn't gone entirely smoothly since then. An initial promise that no new maps would be locked behind paywalls was chucked out the window in February, and Full Circle laid off employees that same month, saying that cutting headcounts means it can "better support Skate's long-term future and focus the team on the things that matter most to you." The end of Skate's seasonal structure is less overtly not good than those moves, but it is a sign that things aren't going quite as Full Circle had envisioned, and the message that it's still "committed to keep driving Skate forward" has a certain 'despite everything' tone that doesn't strike me as the sort of thing you say when when all cylinders are firing. "The game is still a work in progress, and we're using this valuable time to experiment, iterate, and figure out what works best for the long-term health of the game—especially when it comes to social features and progression," the studio wrote. "Ultimately, we want to build Skate in a way that lets us roll out fresh content much faster, even if it's not totally finished yet." Season 5 will end on December 1, after which Full Circle will move to "regular, agile content updates." The end of seasons also means the end of the season pass; the studio is "rethinking how that kind of progression system works." Here's the bullet-point rundown of what's changing: No Seasons, but still regular content updates No skate.Pass or skate.Premium Pass and no Tix At the end of Season 5, the last Auto-Exchange will happen. Any Tix not used on the skate.Pass will be auto-exchanged for any items not yet acquired based on the track you’re on. Once done, any remaining Tix will be wiped. Earnable cosmetics and Quick Drop items through Bounties. All areas will be accessible by everyone via Rip Chips for a 24-hour pass. Isle of Grom: 500 Rip Chips The Stadium: 250 Rip Chips SUMR Camp: 500 Rip Chips (Reminder: Rip Chips can be earned through Bounties or completing Challenges in the world, as well as Spotlight Challenges.) "Moving away from rigid season blocks gives the development team the freedom to launch features earlier in their lifecycle," the studio wrote. "This means we can deploy work-in-progress mechanics and gather your direct feedback to continuously shape and build upon San Vansterdam. We’ve started this with in-game testing of features such as Spot Battles, Block Parties, and Prox Chat before rolling it out officially, and we’re going to continue with this process to ensure we get YOUR feedback on what works/what doesn’t." The 0.331 update to Skate will make a number of other additions and changes as well—full details are up at ea.com but the crash course version is below. New Game Mode: S.K.A.T.E. [New area] RINQ Hotel: Luxury-style street spots. [New area] The Loading Bay of The Vault: Realistic, technical street skating layout. [Updated area] Pump House Park (Grom) Returns [Updated Area] Gullcrest Village Community Parks Visual Update Prox Chat Release QoL Improvements and Bug Fixes (details coming on Nov 30, 2026 via the 0.33.1 patch notes) New Brand Partners: Foundation, Toy Machine, Pig (with brand refreshes from huf, Nike SB, Primitive, Converse, adidas) New Packs: Undead Pack, Undead Deluxe Pack, and adidas Starter Pack New Tracks to the Soundtrack Winter at SUMR Camp Grand Theft Auto 6 GTA 6 guide : One-stop info shop GTA 6 map : The full Vice City tour GTA 6 cheats : A complete list GTA 6 radio : All the songs and stations GTA 6 romance : How to keep a strong bond

title: Witcher 3 Remastered patch has lighting fixes, sign nerfs, and gets rid of a nasty werewolf bug
summary: Turns out they weren't meant to be that hard to kill after all.
content: If you replayed The Witcher 3 in its shiny new remastered form and got absolutely bodied by a couple of werewolf fights you thought were easier back when you had more youthful reflexes, don't worry—the problem wasn't your aging brain and hands after all. It was a bug that's been caught and exterminated in patch 5.02 . "Fixed an issue where werewolves could regenerate health too quickly on higher difficulty settings," the patch notes say, "making them impossible to defeat." Another problem some players had with The Witcher 3 Remastered was its lighting, with interiors in particular looking too dark while some other locations were washed-out flashbangs. Good news: "Fixed various lighting issues across multiple locations and cutscenes," the patch notes say, "including overly bright or dark areas, inconsistent lighting transitions and flickering." They've also "Fixed various lighting issues with hair when Path Tracing is enabled" and "Made various Path Tracing and Ray Reconstruction optimizations and visual improvements, including lighting, shadows, and water rendering." That's all positive stuff, but the balance changes to various signs and mutations will be more controversial. The Remastered version launched with buffs to Witcher signs that made them useful even if you didn't specialize in them, but it may have overdone things a little. This patch walks back some of the potential for you to dominate the entire game with an Aard build, though changes like reducing the Catalyst skill's bonus to Aard and Igni intensity by 10% don't seem like they'll totally change the way you play. I get that people don't like skill nerfs in singleplayer games, but I can also see CD Projekt anticipating next year's Songs of the Past DLC . They don't want to hear a bunch of players say, "It sucked because I trivialized the whole thing with a broken build I got by copying a YouTuber." If some skill nerfs and a reduction to stamina regeneration in combat mean you have to drink more potions to get your signs off, it probably won't ruin your fun. Oh, and if you couldn't complete your Gwent collection because Zoltan Chivay's card didn't show up, the patch notes say it'll now appear in the correct place under the Hanged Man's Tree in Velen. Time to go back and get that 100% achievement at last. title: Good coffee is one of our last comforts in a cruel universe, which is why I'm tempted by this Black Friday coffee grinder deal
summary: The PC in PC Gamer stands for "pourover coffee."
content: Timemore's reengineered S5 Pro flagship manual grinder promises an ideal brew through the power of unprecedented burr geometry. It's got a high capacity for a hand grinder, precision external grind adjustment, and a widened crank knob for easier grinding. Key specs: 30g capacity | 48mm burrs | 15 micron adjustment steps Chestnut S5 Pro price check: Timemore $179.00 View Deal I'll be real with you: There are some days where my morning cup of coffee is the only thing maintaining my tenuous mental wellbeing. Sure, the caffeine offers some chemical assistance for weathering our era's daily whirlwind of psychic damage, but it's more about the ritual: The best way to start the day is by doing something nice for yourself, and there are few things nicer than a good cup of coffee. It makes games better, too. I wrote it on a videogame website and that means it's real. I'm a pourover man myself, but whether you're using a drip machine, moka pot, or French press, nothing will improve the quality of your at-home coffeemaking like grinding your own coffee beans with a respectable grinder like the Timemore Chestnut S5 Pro , currently on sale at 20% off for $143 on Amazon. We're curating all the Black Friday PC gaming deals right here There are two reasons why a good grinder makes for great coffee: First, coffee starts losing the volatile compounds that contribute to its flavor as soon as it's ground, so grinding your beans just before brewing ensures as many of those compounds are contributing to your cup as possible. Second, if your coffee grounds aren't a uniform size, they make an uneven brew: Inconsistently sized grounds—like those produced by cheaper, blade-based grinders that smash the beans apart—means your coffee can be simultaneously underextracted and overextracted, muddying the flavor with all sorts of undesirable notes. A proper hand grinder gives you the best of all worlds: Fresh grounds on demand, quality conical burrs that produce more uniform grind sizes, and a cheaper price point than high-end grinders that might be five to ten times as expensive—or more. I'm in the market for a grinder upgrade myself, and that's why this Black Friday deal on the Timemore Chestnut S5 Pro caught my attention. I've been happily using a cheaper Timemore grinder for a couple of years, so I can already vouch for the brand's quality. The S5 Pro brings some additional features that'd offer some quality-of-life upgrades over my trusty old C2: For one, it's got a bigger capacity. More interesting to me, though, is its precision external grind adjustment with numbered steps. My current grinder's adjustment dial is unlabeled, which can be irritating when I'm switching between coffees. That numbered grind adjustment will make it easier to dial in and keep track of coffee-specific grind sizes. Timemore also boasts that the S5 Pro's reengineered burrs represent "a new benchmark in grinding." And if there's anything I love, it's progress. If that $143 price tag is too expensive of an ask for starting your coffee grinding journey, however, there are similar deals on Timemore's more affordable options: This $60 Chestnut C2S is a great entry point that'll give you a running start towards better coffee. And as we all know, better coffee makes for better gaming. Probably. Do your own research. 👉 Check out all of Amazon's Black Friday coffee grinder deals 👈

title: Physical media is cool again, baby, so drop the needle on some videogame vinyls this Black Friday
summary: Music you can hold in your hands!
content: I am an absolute sucker for physical media—my bookshelves are adorned with generations of console games, I have a CD stash tucked away in my Mum's attic, and I still refuse to buy a Kindle in favour of good ol' fashioned paper and ink. And as we increasingly veer into a more digital age, I've noticed a huge uptick in people yearning to bring their hobbies and collections back into a more tangible form. Music, especially, has seen a huge resurgence in physical popularity. Y'all, my best friend is buying CDs and ripping them onto his PC. Like the good old days! And we've also seen an increasing number of videogame soundtracks make their way onto CD and vinyl, which is something that I am a huge fan of. I love music. I love videogames. I love things I can hold in my hands. It's a triple win! We're curating all the Black Friday PC gaming deals right here Unfortunately, this Black Friday hasn't brought about a ton of good deals on videogame vinyl. But that doesn't mean there aren't little offers to be found here and there. So if you're fixing to expand your physical media collection—or seeking out a gift for the videogame music lover in your life—I've got you covered. If you're looking to scoop up a few albums at once, Target is currently doing a Buy 2 Get 1 Free deal on all its music. It's got a pretty tasty library of videogame OSTs among its 49 pages of soundtrack music, such as: Rockstar Games Grand Theft Auto VI: the Album C418 Minecraft Volume Alpha Jagex Audio Team Runescape: 25 Years Andrew Jeremy Coffee Talk (original Soundtrack) From Software Bloodborne (original Soundtrack) Jeremy Soule The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion (original Soundtrack) Clint Mansell Doom (original Soundtrack) D'Anthoni Wooten Dave the Diver (original Soundtrack) Bethesda Softworks Deathloop (original Soundtrack) Martin O'Donnell Halo 3 (original Soundtrack) Piotr Musial Frostpunk 2 (original soundtrack) Valve Studio Orchestra Fight Songs: The Music of Team Fortress 2 If you're looking for straight-up discounts, that's a little bit of a tougher find. IAm8Bit is doing a small sale on its collection of vinyls, offering between $5 and $15 off some stellar soundtracks like: Machine Girl Neon White Soundtrack Part 1 Studio MDHR Cuphead: The Delicious Last Course Ben Babbitt Kentucky Route Zero Vinyl is still pretty expensive, but hey. If you're clever with your selections at Target you can easily nab a $40 - $50 vinyl for free, and IAm8Bit have great indie options for some bonus purchases that are also a tad cheaper.

title: The canonical USB microphone is still great, and now a total steal for $70
summary: The Blue Yeti is a household name in microphones for a reason.
content: Blue Yeti USB Microphone: was $99.99 now $69.99 I've used a Blue Yeti for nearly a decade and it would happily serve for a decade more. A classic design, good hardware controls, and zero fuss. It's not for true audiophiles, but its quality and affordability are still hard to match all these years later. Key specs: USB A | Four pickup patterns | Hardware gain control Blue Yeti price check: Best Buy $69.99 | Walmart $69.99 View Deal The Blue Yeti might be the most popular USB microphone ever made, and you know what, it earned it. At its usual price, this is a great USB microphone. At $69.99 (its lowest price ever), it's simply one of the best bangs for your buck in this category. The original Blue Yeti released in 2009, and in 17 years it has barely changed. I've had mine for a decade, and as I look around, I'm realizing it is the longest-lasting gadget on my desk. That's because it just works: I plug in, adjust the gain, and my voice comes through clear. These days there are more advanced microphones than the Yeti, like its official sequel the Yeti 2, and certainly mics that are just as competitively priced. Those are good too, and I encourage you to check out cheaper options (like the $26 Amazon Basics mic that we surprisingly love ) before making any decisions. We're curating all the Black Friday PC gaming deals right here But with the Yeti, you absolutely get what it says on the tin. I also think it's still an attractive mic, but it is quite large, so make sure it'll fit on your desk without blocking the corner of your monitor. I've had mine on a mic arm for the past few years, and while it does feel like I'm cosplaying a podcaster just to chill with friends on Discord, it's very convenient. At this price, it's firmly on the high end of "budget" territory while still sounding as good as mics that cost twice as much. If you do use it for long sessions and prefer to keep your mic open, play with the gain levels and make sure software noise cancelling is on in your chat app of choice (Discord's is pretty good out of the box). If that's not enough, consider pairing it with dedicated noise cancelling software like Nvidia Broadcast (assuming your GPU can handle the extra toll). 👉 Check out Amazon's Black Friday gaming mic deals here 👈

title: Microsoft announces it's deprecating the Telnet client in Windows, giving me a sudden flashback to when I used to use Telnet
summary: Just think what you'll be able to do with those extra 156 KB they're freeing up.
content: In its latest update on deprecated features in Windows , Microsoft casually mentioned that "Telnet Client is deprecated and will be removed from Windows in a future release." This may not mean much to you if you didn't do a lot of computer networking in the 1990s or earlier, but the text-based protocol for remotely opening command-line interfaces was a workhorse we used for a bunch of things. It's how antique university lab computers that didn't even have Netscape Navigator installed connected to the internet, how I played text-based online games like the Discworld MUD back in the day, and how we used to connect to our routers. By default, Telnet didn't encrypt all the data it was swapping back and forth between computers, which is why it's since been replaced by tools like SSH and PowerShell. So it's not a surprise that it's being deprecated, and honestly I'm impressed that it outlived both WordPad and Cortana . A Windows feature being deprecated means that it won't be in active development and is a candidate for removal in a future update, so Telnet isn't being 86ed immediately. If you're still using it to test network connections because that's what you're used to then carry on as you were, but get ready to grumble and switch over to PowerShell when Microsoft finally does pull the plug.
